name: Ahmed Elhars - احمد الحارس
note: Family and parenting conversations I come back to. Calm, practical advice on home life without the noise.

name: بتاع اقتصاد
note: Simple Arabic explainers on investing and how money actually works. Good when I want the idea without the jargon.

name: The Immigrant المهاجر
note: An immigrant’s notes on building a life in Canada — the practical parts and the human ones.

name: GLASSROOM جلاس روم
note: Ziad Aladdin’s long conversations with people behind useful ideas. I listen when I want depth, not clips.

name: Veritasium
note: Derek Muller’s science stories that stick. I watch these when I want curiosity more than a tutorial.

name: Mobizil
note: Clear Arabic phone reviews and comparisons. Useful when I just want the tradeoffs, not the hype.

name: Ahmed Hisham Banknote
note: Documentary-style Arabic pieces on markets, investing, and how money moves. Slower, and better for it.

name: المخبر الاقتصادي - Mokhbir Eqtisadi
note: Ashraf Ibrahim makes economics feel readable. I use this when a news headline needs a real explanation.

name: Ahmed Elemam - أحمد الإمام
note: Arabic talks for software engineers — backend, databases, and system design without the fluff.

name: Dansky
note: Adobe and branding lessons that are actually usable. I keep this around for design craft, not trends.

name: Bridges Foundation
note: Fadel Soliman’s calm presentations of Islam to a wider audience. Clear, respectful, and easy to share.

name: Fireship
note: Fast, funny coding videos that still teach something real. Perfect when I want the shape of a topic quickly.

name: هالة سمير
note: Dr. Hala Samir on family, women, and mental health. Grounded advice I trust more than generic self-help.

name: Learn English With TV Series
note: Real English from shows I already like. Helps my ear more than another grammar list.

name: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
note: Beautiful explainers on big questions. I watch when I want the wide view, not a how-to.

name: Rachel's English
note: American English pronunciation, slowly and clearly. I use this when I want my speech to sound more natural.

name: Accent's Way English with Hadar
note: Hadar coaches fluency as a non-native speaker. Honest, kind, and useful when I get stuck on how I sound.

name: محمد الدسوقى - Mohamed El Desouki
note: Computer science and databases taught in Arabic, the university way. Solid when I want fundamentals, not hacks.

name: Theo - t3.gg
note: Theo’s takes on TypeScript, AI, and shipping web apps. Opinionated, current, and good for spotting what matters.

name: Learn English with EnglishClass101.com
note: Short English lessons I can actually finish. Handy for daily practice without opening a course.

name: Mustafa El-Feki - مصطفى الفقي
note: Hardware and tech, explained simply in Arabic. Reviews and teardown-style videos I watch before buying kit.

name: Fouad Sidky - دروس في الفلوس
note: Fouad treats money as decisions, not tips. Practical Arabic finance I actually remember later.

name: MSA
note: Animated personal stories. Light to watch, but some of them stay with me longer than I expect.

name: Tom Bilyeu
note: Long interviews on work, money, and how people think. I skip the hype and keep the useful frames.

name: فاهم بودكاست
note: Arabic conversations that try to wake ideas up, not just fill time. I listen when I want a clearer head.

name: أمجد سمير
note: Amgad’s reminder that changing yourself is the real work. Quiet, serious, and worth sitting with.

name: وعي
note: Hazem, Ahmed, and Sherif talking through ideas out loud. A podcast I put on when I want company with substance.

name: Basem Elewa باسم عليوة
note: Money and accounting through a Shariah lens. Helps me think about finance without splitting it from values.

name: freeCodeCamp.org
note: Long, free courses I still send people to. When I want to learn a stack properly, this is the patient option.

name: Arabic 101
note: Arabic and Quran, taught carefully. I like how they aim for reading with understanding, not just reciting.

name: English with Lucy
note: Lucy’s British English lessons — clear, structured, and easy to fit into a week.

name: 3Blue1Brown
note: Grant Sanderson making math feel visible. I rewatch these when I want intuition, not just formulas.

name: ByteByteGo
note: System design the way the book talks about it — diagrams, tradeoffs, and how big systems actually hold together.

name: Shariah audit- شريعة أوديت
note: Islamic economics and Shariah audit, explained without making it feel locked in a textbook.

name: Ehab Mesallum
note: Dr. Ehab on companies, marketing, and building a healthier Arab business culture. Practical, not slogans.

name: English Fluency Journey
note: Anna learning and teaching English as a non-native speaker. Feels like a study buddy, not a classroom.

name: NetworkChuck
note: Networking, Linux, and IT careers with a lot of energy. Good when I want to touch a tool, not just read about it.

name: بالعربي Big Data
note: Big data topics in Arabic, free and straight. I keep it for the vocabulary as much as the ideas.

name: Tech Vault
note: Deeper tech and career talks for Arabic and English viewers. Useful when I want more than a news recap.

name: Garage Education
note: Science and engineering education with a community feel. I like how they treat curiosity as a public good.

name: Brian Wiles
note: Short educational pieces for any age. Easy to watch, and occasionally they reframe something I thought I knew.

name: Mahmoud Youssef - محمود يوسف
note: Backend, clean code, and system design in Arabic. One of the channels I open when I want that conversation in my language.

name: الشيخ عبدالله كامل - Abdallah Kamel
note: Quran recitation I put on when I want the room to get quiet. Official channel, nothing extra around it.

name: CultRepo
note: Human stories behind open source and AI. I watch these when I want the people, not just the repo.

name: Michael Sambol
note: Data structures and algorithms in a few clean minutes. My go-to when I need a picture of an idea fast.

name: Abu Bakr Soliman
note: Abu Bakr on software work and the career around it, in Arabic. Straight talk from someone who’s built things.

name: storybooth
note: Teens telling their own stories. Raw, sometimes heavy, and a reminder that people are more than their highlight reel.

name: Passionate Coders | محمد المهدي
note: Mohamed Elmahdy teaching programming with patience. Arabic lessons I recommend when someone wants to start properly.

name: Net Ninja
note: Shaun’s web dev playlists — the ones I still use when I want a clean path through a library or framework.

name: pragma
note: Yasser Elsayed on software craft after years at big companies. Arabic, senior, and light on theater.

name: Hussein Nasser
note: Hussein making backend, networking, and databases feel concrete. I learn more from his examples than from slides.

name: Mohamed Elsherif
note: Software engineering talks and the occasional podcast. Mohamed says the quiet part about the job out loud.

name: Caleb Curry
note: Caleb keeps programming simple without talking down. Good beginner-to-middle ground when I want a friendly reset.

name: linguamarina
note: Marina’s English-learning vlogs. Casual enough to watch at night, useful enough that phrases stick.

name: Abdul Bari
note: Algorithms explained slowly, on a whiteboard. Still one of the best ways I know to actually understand them.

name: Elzero Tube
note: Osama Elzero’s second shelf — extra lessons and clips around the main Web School path.

name: The Cherno
note: Yan building Hazel and teaching C++ in public. I watch when I want systems-level thinking, not another web stack.

name: Christopher Okhravi
note: Design patterns and abstractions, taught like he really wants you to get them. Dense, in a good way.

name: MIT OpenCourseWare
note: Full MIT courses, free. I don’t binge this — I open it when I want the real lecture, not a summary.

name: Arabic Competitive Programming
note: Mostafa Saad’s problem-solving path. The channel I point to when someone wants competitive programming done seriously.

name: Fekra - Sohaib Aldosoky
note: Sohaib on motion design and freelancing. Arabic, generous, and useful if you want to get paid for creative work.

name: Ali Muhammad Ali
note: Ali sharing whatever useful thing he just learned. Wide range, always aimed at helping someone get through a hard bit.

name: The English Coach
note: Stefanie coaching independent English learners. Direct, adult, and focused on sounding like yourself.

name: anaHr
note: Arabic HR and workplace talk. Helps me see the people side of work, not only the engineering one.

name: Benny Productions
note: Photoshop and digital art with a lot of craft. I open this when I want to get better at the tool, not collect presets.

name: Arabhardware - عرب هاردوير
note: The Arabic hardware community I grew up reading. Reviews and PC talk with actual standards.

name: طحالب
note: Egyptian commentary I watch to stay close to the culture and the jokes — not everything has to be a lesson.

name: محمد خيال - Mohamed Khayal
note: Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign in Arabic. Practical design lessons I can apply the same day.

name: Dr.Ebtsam Alqadi - ابتسام القاضي
note: A calm space for Muslim women on identity and living with a quieter heart. Thoughtful more than loud.

name: Elzero Web School
note: Osama Elzero’s main path for web development in Arabic. Still the playlist I send first.

name: zAmericanEnglish
note: Ibrahim’s full path from beginner English to fluency. I like that it doesn’t assume you already paid for a course.

name: EPIC HARDWARE
note: PC hardware reviews and news in Arabic. Good companion to Arabhardware when I want another honest take.

name: Kevin Nanns
note: Enterprise networking from someone who designs those systems. I watch when I want the architecture, not a cert cram.

name: Yehia Tech
note: Yahya on architecture and leadership after years of building. Senior engineering talk without the LinkedIn polish.
